Which is a a way uh bigger project than adding a few percent of Bitcoin to a portfolio. And so that's what's happening. It's brought, frankly, a bunch of investors certainly that previously had no Bitcoin or crypto exposure into Bitcoin, but it's also brought a lot of investors into ETFs for the first time that maybe they they did hold and trade stocks before, but they'd never held ETFs. And obviously we're big believers, as I know you are, in the incredible power of ETFs to deliver low-cost diversified portfolios to investors and ultimately tremendous long-term financial empowerment and outcome. So I think it's been actually a really nice story in both directions. >> Doesn't sound like we're going to get a day in the life video on your Instagram account anytime soon. >> That wouldn't be that interesting anyway. >> [laughter] >> Let's talk about midterms and regulation. Obviously there's a lot of folks who are waiting till tonight, and they're going to figure out, you know, who ends up winning this thing. Does it have any impact on your strategy flows or maybe even future product launches? >> Not really, to be honest. I think that particularly for the larger more established assets. If you think about Bitcoin, if you think about Ether, um there there's a a pretty good clarity over uh what you can and can't do today already, right? And Bitcoin has a lot of what it needs uh already. And um you know we've seen even with clarity breaking down the SEC has been incredibly proactive and thoughtful in engaging with the ecosystem and trying to come up with um you know opportunities to help accommodate and accelerate responsible innovation. And I certainly think that's going to continue regardless of of what happens. >> And then lastly just from a regulatory standpoint um it does feel like this administration is pro the technology in general. Um do you worry that future administrations, whether Republican or Democrat, may be less excited or less kind of leaned forward? And do you start preparing for that now or is it just hey let's play the cards as they're dealt, you know, two years, four years, six years from now? >> Yeah, well I think it actually falls back to any industry, whether that's digital assets or AI or otherwise, to effectively prove itself as very economically useful and societally beneficial. And the more you do that, the more you drive adoption, the more you drive real value add use cases, um the more it becomes a uh bipartisan issue and not something that uh you know will swing back between various administrations. So I think it's you know it's a really critical time for the digital asset space uh to uh you know uh use this this moment and um you know the the uh very supportive uh SEC, CFTC who've been um you know very constructive in in dealing with the ecosystem and allow that to help flourish um lots of great adoption and real value add use cases. >> Well I think you guys are doing a fantastic job and the results speak for itself. So I appreciate you coming and uh Robbie Mitzner everybody. >> Thank you.
